title: The Seven Sins of Memory: How the Mind Forgets and Remembers
author: Daniel L. Schacter
note: Selected for Alan A. Stone's enthusiastic American Journal of Psychiatry review, APA recognition, and substantial positive reader reception (Goodreads 3.88/1,900; corroborating detailed reader appraisal). This is research explanation, not primarily memory-improvement advice. Stone finds the final evolutionary interpretation weaker than the experimental exposition. That objection is retained: adaptive explanations are hypotheses, not established causes for every memory error. Inspected criticism does not justify high-confidence veto of the book's empirical framework. Broad reader praise is qualified rather than unanimous.
notes: Substantial experimental foundation; evolutionary explanations are less secure than the classification of errors.
Connects cognition, attention, neural evidence and real-world testimony.
Useful for evaluating recollection, source attribution and decision records.
Explains different failure mechanisms instead of treating memory as a single faculty.

D=8, moderate confidence from Stone's detailed review, published excerpt and reader reports. Distinct error classes add mechanisms; the final evolutionary synthesis is less persuasive. No full-text audit.
Core distinctions remain useful; older examples are historical rather than current clinical guidance.
Useful scientific and inferential content, with limited direct industrial relevance.
Leading memory researcher with strong specialist reception.
Clear cumulative taxonomy illustrated by concrete cases.
Accessible and generally disciplined exposition.

title: Evolution's Bite: A Story of Teeth, Diet, and Human Origins
author: Peter S. Ungar
note: Selected for the favorable Inquisitive Biologist review, Ann Gibbons's publisher-reproduced endorsement and positive reader reception (Goodreads 3.94/122, including substantive reports). A research narrative explaining inference from teeth, not a specialist dentistry curriculum or nutrition-advice book. The brief dietary conclusion does not determine its dominant purpose. Climate, feeding ecology and human adaptation are central, so T11 applies. Broad evolutionary timespan through modern consequences has no single historical endpoint. A creationist criticism was inspected; its appeal to the Genesis flood does not establish reasoned specialist foundational criticism under V9. No serious veto established from the inspected evidence.
notes: Explains fossil evidence and uncertainty in reconstructing diets; historical hypotheses are distinguished from observations.
Connects tooth mechanics, chemistry, climate, food availability and human development.
Useful model of triangulating indirect evidence and separating possible from actual behavior.
Explains wear, morphology and dietary constraints with causal detail.

D=8, moderate confidence from the detailed biologist review and substantive reader reports. Methods and changing ecological constraints add distinct learning; early technical detail can slow reading. No full-text audit.
Scientific methods and historical development remain durable.
Scientific inference and biological mechanisms fit partly; little industrial application.
Research specialist in dental anthropology and human evolution.
Clear progression from methods to synthesis; technical opening requires attention.
Accessible explanation with careful distinctions.
